issues.legal_issue: A delay in filing a first appeal should be condoned when the appellant bona fide prosecuted the appeal in a court lacking jurisdiction because of a mistaken belief, and the circumstances establish sufficient cause.
material_facts: The appellant pursued the appeal before a district court that lacked jurisdiction, believing that it was the proper court.
The jurisdictional error escaped notice both when the appeal was instituted and during its hearing.
The appellant then filed the appeal in the High Court late, and the respondent conceded that excluding the time spent in the district court would make it timely.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have condoned the delay. The Supreme Court set aside its refusal, condoned the delay, and remanded the first appeal for disposal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, delay may be condoned where sufficient cause is established. Bona fide prosecution of an appeal before a court lacking jurisdiction, in circumstances where the mistake escaped scrutiny, can constitute sufficient cause; the period so spent may be excluded when assessing whether the appeal was timely. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: first_appeal_delay_case and bona_fide_wrong_forum_prosecution and jurisdiction_error_escaped_review and excluded_period_restores_timeliness

predicates.first_appeal_delay_case: The matter concerns an application to excuse delay in filing a first appeal.
predicates.bona_fide_wrong_forum_prosecution: The appellant pursued the appeal in a court that lacked jurisdiction because the appellant bona fide believed it was the proper court.
predicates.jurisdiction_error_escaped_review: The jurisdictional mistake was not noticed when the appeal was instituted or while it was heard.
predicates.excluded_period_restores_timeliness: Excluding the time spent pursuing the appeal in the court lacking jurisdiction makes the appeal timely.

issues.definition: When an application concerns delay in a first appeal, the appellant bona fide pursued it in the wrong court, that mistake escaped review, and excluding that period restores timeliness, the delay is condoned.
